content.title: City of Arvada awarded $100,000 Colorado Gives Foundation grant to support continuation of Suburban Studios program
content.summary: The City of Arvada has been awarded a $100,000 grant from the Colorado Gives Foundation to support the Suburban Studios program, which provides transitional housing and support services for individuals exiting homelessness. The funding will enable the continuation of these services, which have already helped 125 people secure housing since January 2025. The City aims to assist 65 individuals experiencing homelessness in Olde Town Arvada by the end of 2026 as part of its broader strategy to address homelessness in the community.
content.body:
Arvada, CO – The City of Arvada has received a $100,000 Housing Grant from Colorado Gives Foundation. The award is intended to support efforts by nonprofit organizations and government entities in Jefferson County to increase affordable housing options and provide transitional housing opportunities and navigation for individuals exiting homelessness.

The City's Homelessness Response team will use the funds to continue transitional housing and support services provided at the Suburban Studios extended-stay hotel. Initially made possible by a grant from the Colorado Department of Local Affairs (DOLA), the Suburban Studios program provides temporary shelter and case management for Arvadans experiencing homelessness.

"The Suburban Studios program has been changing lives for people experiencing housing insecurity in Arvada," said Lynette Badasarian, the City's Homelessness Program Manager. "This grant means we can continue to utilize that transformative resource in the citywide effort to reduce homelessness."

The City partners in this work with numerous organizations, including Mission Arvada – an Olde Town Arvada day shelter and housing navigation center that also received a $100,000 grant from Colorado Gives Foundation. The collaboration has seen progress, particularly where Suburban Studios is concerned: Since January 2025, 125 people have left the Suburban Studios program into housing.

"Suburban gives people stability, along with accountability and help in areas like career coaching, housing navigation, and peer support to help them get back on their feet," Badasarian explained. "Often, people are moving into apartments without the help of vouchers when they leave, because having a roof over their heads and support and connection during a difficult time helped them secure or hold onto full-time jobs."

Suburban Studios is one thread in the fabric of Arvada's coordinated response to homelessness. One of the City of Arvada's priority goals for 2026 focuses on another aspect of the effort, said City Manager Don Wick. "Addressing homelessness in our community is an imperative for all of us. To meet that imperative, the City has a goal of helping 65 people experiencing homelessness in Olde Town Arvada into housed outcomes by the end of 2026.

"Having an option like Suburban Studios available makes meeting that aspiration attainable for the City and our community partners," Wick added. As of April, Mission Arvada, Family Tree, Safeside Recovery, and other organizations have helped 25 people experiencing homelessness in Olde Town into housing, in addition to 14 people who have moved off the street into a 24/7 shelter.

To learn more about how the City of Arvada is addressing homelessness, and to sign up for a monthly newsletter on our efforts, visit the City of Arvada website at [arvadaco.gov/homelessness](http://arvadaco.gov/homelessness).

[Colorado Gives Foundation](https://coloradogivesfoundation.org/) is a community foundation (a public charity, 501(c)3) dedicated to improving the lives of people in Jefferson County and supporting Jeffco nonprofits through philanthropy tools including grantmaking.
